title: Global Temp view shows up empty when passed from Pyspark to Scala notebook in Databricks
question:
I have a Azure Databricks workflow which runs a Pyspark notebook which in turns calls a Scala notebook(legacy) for a list of tables. In Pyspark notebook, I save a Dataframe to a GlobalTempView and pass the name to the scala notebook.

#pyspark notebook
df = read_from_database()
df.createOrReplaceGlobalTempView("view_name")

result = dbutils.notebook.run(
                notebook_path, timeout, {
                "input_view": "global_temp.view_name"
          })

When I try to read the GlobalTempView in the scala notebook, for some tables, view looks empty. Schema exists but no data.

//scala notebook
var df = spark.table("global_temp.view_name")

I eventually got it to work when I cached dataframe before creating the view in Pyspark, then the data shows up in scala notebook.

#pyspark notebook
df = read_from_database()
df.cache()
df.createOrReplaceGlobalTempView("view_name")

Can somebody help me understand why this would happen only for certain tables and always the same tables?

PS: The tables that doesn't work doesn't have any special schema or data types than the ones that work.
answer:
This happens because spark evaluates dataframes lazily when you create a global temp view without an action, the underlying data may not be materialized yet.for some tables, the query plan might push the read downstream, so the scala notebook sees only the schema.
caching forces materialization that’s why adding .cache() before the view works consistently.
